name: voxtral-3B-atc-transcribe
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507 (config.json max_position_embeddings 131072). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-06. A full fine-tune of mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507 for air-traffic-control radio transcription, not a new base model: 4.676B identical tensor set, config inherited unchanged. ~7 epochs / 23h on one RTX 3090 Ti, trained on the jacktol/ATC-ASR-Dataset train+validation splits and the jlvdoorn/atcosim training split. Recorded because the card's WER table puts this model and the untrained base in the same row on both ATC test sets (8.0% vs 105.6% typical noise, 1.3% vs 83.2% low noise). Read the gap carefully: WER above 100% means the untrained base emits more tokens than the reference contains, so most of this is domain adaptation to a very narrow vocabulary rather than general ASR skill - the card's own comparison to jacktol's Whisper ATC tune (6.5%, reported not re-run) shows how little headroom is left. Licence apache-2.0, no repo creation date published.

benchmarks.name: Typical noise (jacktol/ATC-ASR-Dataset test)
benchmarks.config: Card WER table '| Dataset | this model | untrained base |': 8.0% vs untrained base 105.6% on the same test split. Lower is better. Fine-tune = ~7 epochs / 23h on one RTX 3090 Ti, trained on the ATC-ASR training+validation splits and the jlvdoorn/atcosim training split. Card prints no beam, VAD or normalisation settings.

benchmarks.name: Low noise (jlvdoorn/atcosim validation)
benchmarks.config: Same card table: this model 1.3% vs untrained base 83.2% on the atcosim validation split. Lower is better. Card prints a comparison to tclin/whisper-large-v3-turbo-atcosim-finetune at 3.7% (reported, not re-run).
